summary: Ferry County, WA tower built 1933 (55-ft pole tower, 6x6 cab); removed or destroyed in 1952; tower site has no footings, road access good for all vehicles.

facts.design: 55-foot pole tower with 6x6 foot cab and log cabin
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1952 (register says removed; Willhite and firelookout.com say destroyed). Willhite reports no tower footings and the structure crashed in the woods

staffing.status: Known lookout personnel: Paul Taylor (1923) and James Kasmer (1945); no fuller roster in the sources read

access.note: Forest road from Curlew; Willhite says good for all vehicles; trailhead is a berm with parking for a few cars and no sign

visit.trail_note: The old road to the site is the trail; the tower spot is on the highest knoll with no views and the cabin spot on a smaller knoll with views (Willhite)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower and cabin were removed in 1952; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed that year. The story reports both and does not pick one.

The register and the firelookout.org list both give 48.96063, -118.68375, which the record uses. The other pair in the brief's conflict note (48.9891, -118.6489) comes from a source not read in this run, so it is not used.

A 1915 newspaper item says lookout towers were built on Vulcan, while the register and Willhite date the surviving tower to 1933. The sources do not say whether the 1915 towers were the same. The story gives the 1915 item and the 1933 date without linking them.

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' is now public (Forest road, trailhead with parking). The 1915 item is kept as a separate event because the sources do not link it to the 1933 tower. Coordinates in the record match the register and the firelookout.org list; the West US Lookouts pair was not read. Willhite's 2019 photo captions are the only description of the site today. Read 4 pages and ran 1 websearch.
